title: Steam Fish with Hollandaise Sauce
description: A refined Continental seafood dish featuring delicately steamed white fish served with silky Hollandaise sauce, seasonal vegetables, and fresh herb garnishes.

ingredients.title: For the Fish
items: Fresh white fish fillets (sea bass, cod, or snapper) – 2 pieces (160–180 g each)
Freshly ground white pepper – to taste

ingredients.title: For the Hollandaise Sauce
items: Unsalted butter, melted and clarified – 125 g
Cayenne pepper or white pepper – a pinch

ingredients.title: For the Garnish
items: Baby carrots, blanched and sautéed in butter

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Fish
steps: Lightly season the fish fillets with salt and white pepper.
Brush with olive oil and place each fillet on a small square of parchment or banana leaf.
Add a lemon slice and a sprig of dill or tarragon over each fillet.
Steam at 85–90°C (185–195°F) for 6–8 minutes until the fish is opaque and just begins to flake.
Avoid over-steaming to maintain a moist and delicate texture.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Prepare the Hollandaise Sauce
steps: Place egg yolks and white wine vinegar in a heatproof bowl over a barely simmering bain-marie.
Whisk continuously until the mixture becomes pale, thick, and slightly ribbon-like.
Slowly drizzle in warm clarified butter while whisking constantly to create a smooth emulsion.
Season with salt, lemon juice, and cayenne pepper or white pepper.
Keep warm at approximately 60°C (140°F) and avoid overheating.
Adjust consistency with a teaspoon of warm water if the sauce becomes too thick.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Plating & Presentation
steps: Place the steamed fish slightly off-center on a warm white porcelain plate.
Spoon Hollandaise sauce generously over the fish.
Arrange sautéed vegetables beside the fish in an elegant manner.
Drizzle with lemon zest oil for aromatic freshness.
Finish with microgreens, chervil leaves, or a small sprig of dill.
Add sea salt flakes just before serving for a refined finish.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot as an elegant Continental seafood main course.
Pair with steamed asparagus, French beans, or buttered seasonal vegetables.
Serve on white porcelain plates for a refined restaurant-style presentation.
WinePairing- White Burgundy (Chardonnay) or Sancerre (Sauvignon Blanc)

chefTips: Use gentle moist steam to preserve the fish’s natural tenderness.
Hollandaise should be silky and warm, never hot, to prevent splitting.
Pass the sauce through a fine mesh strainer for an ultra-smooth texture.
Use high-quality butter and fresh herbs for the best flavor.
